balloon_maker.text: Bristol's been making hot-air balloons since the 1960s. A lot of the world's balloons were stitched round here.
The first people to fly in one went up over Paris in 1783, in a balloon made by the Montgolfier brothers. Paper and silk, and a straw fire.

then.text: Envelope's with Gwen? Good. Tell her to stop landing in hawthorn hedges.

else.text: Gwen's envelope! All patched. Two thousand square metres of rip-stop nylon, and she put a hole in it with a hedge.
Quick question before I hand it over: why does a hot-air balloon go up?
Why does a hot-air balloon rise?

then.text: Spot on! Hot air spreads out, so the envelope's full of air lighter than the air around it. It floats, like a cork in water.
You received Gwen's balloon envelope. It's enormous, and somehow fits in the bag.

else.text: Not quite! Think about what happens when you heat air. Try me again.
